source_text: Nec ea hominibus praeciperet, quae per naturam eorum sciret non posse servari, nec pro rebus naturalibus reum quempiam iudicaret.
pass_a_gloss: Nor would he command to humans those things which he knew through their nature cannot be kept, nor would he judge anyone a defendant for natural things.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: He would not command people to do things he knew their nature made them unable to observe; nor would he judge anyone guilty for what belongs to their nature.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
